name: Pacific South Subsurface Countercurrent
scope: Declared historical southern mean-core studied reach from 155 W 3.5 S to 110 W 5.5 S. These gates truncate the larger southern subsurface flow. Western formation, secondary-jet geometry and eastern continuation are excluded. This is one study-defined connection, not an aggregate centerline or sum of primary and secondary branches.
layer: Southern subsurface/Tsuchiya flow. Johnson and Moore (1997) Table 1 gives local mean peak depths 250 m at 155 W and 160 m at 110 W; no uniform depth or full vertical bounds imposed. Later observations resolve primary and deeper secondary jets; their correspondence to this historical mean-core route remains a review gate.
time_convention: Editorial connection of Johnson and Moore (1997) mean section support from a historical 1967-1996 CTD compilation. No exact regional observation dates, annual mean measured axis or monthly geometry reconstructed. Rowe et al. (2000) branch observations are separate context, not a second route or annual evolution series.
source_locator: Sections 2-3 and Table 1: south SSCC peaks at 155 W 3.5 S/250 m and 110 W 5.5 S/160 m. Latitude integration bands are not widths. Rowe et al. (2000), introduction and section 3e/Fig. 10 caption, distinguish primary and secondary southern jets.
source_citation: Johnson and Moore (1997), The Pacific Subsurface Countercurrents and an Inertial Model, Journal of Physical Oceanography 27, 2448-2459.
source_license: NOAA-hosted article states not subject to U.S. copyright; published by AMS in 1997. Regional facts paraphrased; source figures and historical CTD fields not packaged.
coordinate_selection: OSW uses rounded Table 1 mean-core neighborhoods at 155 W 3.5 S and 110 W 5.5 S as truncation gates. Intermediate 140 W 4.2 S and 125 W 4.8 S are editor-selected. No source figure, current axis or dated particle path digitized. Correspondence with later primary/secondary branch labels is not assumed.

alternative_routes.interpretation: OSW equatorward bend assumption, not a seasonal path or width edge.
OSW poleward bend assumption, not a secondary-jet path or width edge.

scenario_rule: Three declared shapes crossed with uniform longitude offsets -0.25/0/+0.25 and independent endpoint-latitude offsets -0.25/0/+0.25 degrees: 81 editorial cases, not width bounds, seasonal extrema or confidence intervals.
remaining_gates: Review correspondence of historical mean-core sections to later primary/secondary labels; no branch aggregation inferred.
Review interpolation with compatible southern-jet velocity fields and independently resolve secondary-jet geometry.
Obtain month/depth axes before seasonal dimensions; source compilation years are not route observation dates.
Resolve western formation and eastern continuation; transport bands and PV-front spans must remain separate from current width.
route_extent_kind: 155 W to 110 W historical southern mean-core reach

supporting_sources.citation: Rowe, Firing and Johnson (2000), Pacific Equatorial Subsurface Countercurrent Velocity, Transport, and Potential Vorticity, JPO 30, 1172-1187.
supporting_sources.locator: Introduction pp. 1172-1174; data methods pp. 1174-1176; section 3e/Fig. 10 caption p. 1183.
supporting_sources.role: Primary/secondary naming and unresolved splitting/independent origin; front scale is not whole-current width. No route digitized from figures.
supporting_sources.license_note: PDF states AMS copyright; no open license inferred; figures and data not packaged.

method: Sum shortest WGS84 geodesic distances between successive OSW editorial vertices; no velocity field or current core is reconstructed.
map_land_check: All 81 routes, geodesically densified at spacing no greater than 10 km, avoid the coarse OSW atlas land mask in display coordinates. This is not a shelf-break, reef, bathymetric or high-resolution land-clearance verification.
state_relation_role: Editorial line/display-region crossing; physical current passage unresolved.
